The first it misses is '6ade180c.2d0ea2e2 0x7540ed1336c0 conn=1002 op=1 SEARCH RESULT tag=101 err=0 qtime=0.000015 etime=0.001110 nentries=3 text='. Of the 7 patterns, the closest to it is '%{BASE16NUM:timestamp} %{DATA:thread} conn=%{INT:conn} fd=%{INT:fd} ACCEPT from IP=%{IP:client_ip}:%{INT:client_port} \\('. the pattern matches up to %{DATA:thread}, which fails on '.2d0ea2e2 0x7540ed1336c0 conn=1002 op=1 '. The capture before it, %{BASE16NUM:timestamp}, matched only '6ade180c' and stopped at '.2d0ea2e2 0x' - it is too narrow, and that is the one to widen It also misses lines of other shapes: '6ade180b.32beb5e3 0x7540ed1336c0 conn=1001 op=0 RESULT tag=97 err=49 qtime=0.000022 etime=0.000201 text='; '6ade180a.373d7986 0x7540ed9346c0 conn=1000 op=0 RESULT tag=97 err=0 qtime=0.000012 etime=0.000225 text='; '6ade180d.27845bc8 0x7540ed1336c0 conn=1003 op=0 RESULT tag=97 err=0 qtime=0.000011 etime=0.000125 text='. If this line is a VARIANT of the others - an extra word, a field that is sometimes absent - make that part optional with (?:...)? rather than writing a second pattern. If it is a DIFFERENT KIND of message - different words, not one more of them - add a pattern for it to `alternatives`, reusing the same capture name for the same value.
